column1: # away from a GPU that was doing it four times faster. Correct answer
# machine. Prompt work at 512 tokens belongs on the RX 560 (313 t/s) and no CPU
# kernel is going to beat that; generation is memory-bound and stays a CPU job
# which is why the tg column is unharmed.
# So `supports_op` accepting a shape must ALSO mean "and this is the right
# device for it". Today it only means the first half. The fix is for the backend
# to decline large-batch matmuls when a GPU device is present and would take
# them -- roughly the inverse of the size gate in patch 0003
# stop the fork declining work it SHOULD take.
# Until that lands: run CPU-only configurations with this fork
# enable it for hybrid offload.
# HOW TO READ THE VERDICT COLUMN. Four different failures have produced
# plausible-looking numbers in this project
#   VOID:bulldnn-never-ran        the arm named "+bulldnn" did not run it
#   VOID:bulldnn-ran-in-baseline  the control was contaminated
#   VOID:implied-NNNGFLOPS...     a CPU-only arm exceeded what a CPU can do
#                                 i.e. the GPU computed it
# implied_gflops is 2 * params * tokens/s. The threshold is 400
# peak -- the fp32 ceiling here is ~106 and these INT8 kernels legitimately
# reach 137 -- but a bar set between "fast CPU" and "obviously a GPU" (~1300).
# The device flag that engages the fork DIFFERS BY BOX: -dev none suffices on
# this machine
column2: while the A10 needs -dev ZenDNN. Same sources
